entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2987)
release_notes: Prepares customizable color themes and high-contrast appearance support for upcoming extensions, with no change to current app behavior.
Prepares the sandboxed plugin helper runtime and bundle signing checks for upcoming plugin extensions, with no change to current app behavior.
Remembering a voice in a one-on-one Zoom call no longer asks whether the speaker is one person.
Internal.
Choose from ten visual themes in Settings under App.
Using VoiceOver or another assistive app on the New Project name field no longer reloads the window.
Using VoiceOver or another assistive app on the meeting name no longer reloads the meeting window.
Scrolling to the top of a live transcript keeps your place and Jump to Latest instead of returning to the newest words.
A meeting's suggested Ask questions now show before you ask anything.
VoiceOver now reads Home as the window's main content, and each project on Home as a button you can press.
Sidebar buttons stay readable at larger text sizes, and a meeting's "…" menu no longer covers its time while open.
Create a project with an optional description directly from a meeting's Project menu
When you rename a speaker, a meeting from another Mac shows that name in its summary.
Transcription stays on this Mac. Summaries and questions can still use a hosted model.
Transcripts align more consistently, summary sections have clearer spacing, and long meeting statuses and voice prompts remain readable.
The live transcript stays with the newest words while you record until you scroll up to read earlier lines, and Jump to Latest reliably brings you back.
Renaming a Zoom speaker after remembering their voice updates their detected words too.
Meetings just after midnight now appear under the date they start.

Removing a pinned line in **Before you finish** now updates the notes editor immediately even when the notes field holds focus, and leaves the sealed meeting summary settled so **Last time** on the next meeting in the series keeps its summary.
An edited or dismissed action item stays edited or gone when you copy the summary, publish the notes, or look at last time.
When you start a new meeting on this Mac while Auldera is still writing the previous meeting's summary, that summary now finishes in the background instead of stopping.
Live meeting summaries now address you directly in the second person instead of treating your speaker label as a third-person name.
Choose System, Light, or Dark appearance in Settings under App.
Scrollbars stay hidden in the sidebar and menus, and appear as a subtle rounded pill in the notes and transcript panes only while you hover or edit.
Suggested counts stay aligned across Home, Projects, and Review after you add a meeting to a project.
Meeting summaries for longer calls finish faster when a summary pass needs to shorten its bullets to fit.
Action items now show the right owner when a commitment starts with "You will" or names a group, and format owners the same way across meetings.
Meeting reminder cards now match the Light and Dark design board with the app icon, start-time copy, and inline action buttons.
The note that confirms a meeting was added to a project now puts a dot before its Undo link, and a filing note or refusal followed by a link omits its trailing period before the dot.
Auldera checks for updates when it opens and lets you install a new version before starting meeting detection or setup.
Home stays responsive while meeting countdowns update.
No user-visible change: this adds the Suggested Projects journey tests.
Removing a pin during pin review no longer causes the "You edited this meeting" notice to reappear after relaunching the app.

You can describe several projects at once from Improve Suggested Projects, so Auldera suggests the right project for more of your meetings. It opens from a meeting's project menu and from the Not in a project page.
Right now, the live line that says what the meeting is about, now speaks to you correctly: "You are proposing…" instead of "You is proposing…".

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2918)
release_notes: The app bundle now carries the licences of open-source components vendored inside FluidAudio and MLX Swift.
While a meeting records, the Summary's waiting line now says the first lines appear after a few minutes of talk, matching when they really show up.
Home and Projects now show how many meetings have a suggested project, and Review lets you add or dismiss each suggestion in one place.

A pin now captures one person's sentence from the moment you pinned, instead of everything said in the last 30 seconds. Answers to your questions about a meeting or project now state the answer directly.
A note you add while a meeting's summary is still being written now reaches the meeting. It shows in exports, and the summary says it is out of date.
Deleting a meeting on another device now also cleans up its action item edits and checkmarks on this Mac.
Add a short description to any project, when you create it or on its page, so Auldera can use it to suggest which meetings belong there.
When a meeting ends, or when you update a project description or your meeting notes, Auldera checks in the background whether recent unfiled meetings match one of your projects.
In a meeting's project menu, type to find any project, including archived ones, see how many meetings each holds, and pick one or start a new project from what you typed, all from the keyboard.
Live notes now appear during a recording on every Mac, and the page says why when they can't.
Meetings can now suggest a project in the header menu, with one-click Add, Undo, and Dismiss.
No user-facing change: this fixes the design screenshot checks and a design note.

Tags are gone from Auldera on the Mac: no Tags menu on a meeting, no Tag filter in search, and no Tags group in Settings. Search finds meetings by title, date, people and Project. Meetings you already tagged keep their tags.
Live meeting summaries keep updating for longer on Macs that are short on memory.
Meeting reminders now appear as a banner at the top of your screen, with one click to join and record.
The app bundle now carries the licence notices of the open-source packages Auldera links beneath its direct dependencies, and Sentry's third-party notices.
Recording settings now show the notice switch the way the design draws it, and the crash-report privacy line sits under its switch.
In Send Feedback, a longer attachment label wraps onto its own lines instead of crowding the next row, and ticked boxes now show a check mark.
Rewriting a project summary now shows that it's working, and tells you if it couldn't finish.

A meeting that is in no project now shows the same "+ Project" button before, during and after the meeting. The "Saved to no project" note, a stray "—" in the just-finished header, and a false "You edited this meeting" note after you review your pins are gone.
The recording widget's level bars now move with the sound, it names the meeting, and it opens centred at the top of the screen instead of over the window's Stop and Pin.
Back now returns you to the meeting after you press Home, and projects get their "where things stand" summary on every Mac.
The Privacy page now explains what Markdown files are, project colours in Settings read larger, and the Calendar step in first-run setup says Allow Access.
Home's Coming up now counts down to your next meeting ("in 40 min") in the hour before it starts, as the sidebar does.

What's New now shows the date each version came out. The About, Update and What's New windows are the size the design draws, as tall as their content, and the Update window no longer opens with a ring around its checkbox.
The sidebar now counts down to your next meeting ("in 40 min") in the hour before it starts, and its Join button keeps working while you are recording another meeting.
The dot for a project with no colour and the marker beside today's date in Coming up now match the design's colours.
In the on-device-only build, Settings no longer offers a cloud route that did nothing. AI says that transcription and summaries run on this Mac.
The About window now credits every open-source component Auldera ships with, each with the licence it is published under, and the app bundle carries their licence notices.
During a recording, the Summary now shows a short line about what people are talking about right now, written on your Mac.
Add a short description to any project—either when creating it or on the project's page—so Auldera can use it to suggest which meetings belong in that project.
Ask can now answer questions about prices and quantities that someone stated in the meeting.

The sidebar search, the speaker-naming card, the summary bullets and the top bar in a narrow window now line up with the design to the pixel. The search field no longer has a clear button; press Esc to clear it.
No change for current testers. December builds can find updates without an account.
Import transcripts now shows the Project choice on its own row below your files, the way the design draws it, and files every imported meeting in the Project you pick.
None: test-only.

Settings follows the new design: AI says where transcription and summaries run and which model each uses, Projects shows how many meetings each Project holds, App lists automatic and beta updates, and Advanced shows how much space your meetings take.
No change for current testers. Adds the build switch for the December local-only release.
A project's Next line shows its next meeting up to three weeks out, and a project summary written today or yesterday says so.

Recording and Calendar settings now follow the new design: Record automatically and Microphone sit together, Remembered voices come first with a count, and each calendar account shows how many calendars you watch and opens them in one tap.
Your notes stay open and editable while the final summary is written.
Show All in a meeting's Brief now fills the Brief with every earlier meeting by month, with Show Less at the top.
The menu bar menu is simpler and matches the rest of the app: it shows what's next on your calendar, and Quit now asks before it stops a recording.
The About window now credits the open-source libraries Auldera is built with, each with the licence it is published under.
Menus highlight the row you are on in the accent color, and their rows are easier to read and to hit.
Transcripts now show each speaker's time by default, and the time stays on as you move between meetings.

Meeting pages sit a little closer to their designs: the recording dot, the notes formatting bar, the Notes, Brief and Transcript switch, and the Back and Forward buttons now line up exactly, and the Join and Record dot reads clearly in dark mode.
Searching the sidebar now offers Projects, a Last 30 days range and the typed text, shows the matches under one count with their dates, and tucks Go to and Coming up away while it does.
A recording that is not in a project now shows an Add Project button under its title, its menu offers Pin, and a new recording's summary says when its points will start to appear.
Show All on Home opens the Projects page. Back returns to Projects from a project opened there, and Forward returns to a project's Ask tab.
After you stop a recording, you can keep typing in your notes while it finishes saving, and the meeting header says it just ended.
Settings has a new look: a Settings heading, a title on each pane, and quieter menus and buttons.
During a recording, the timer and Stop in the top bar now sit in one quiet pill, meeting titles are a little larger in wide windows, and the live transcript no longer fades older words.
Buttons, fields and rows have slightly rounder corners, as in the design.
None. No user-facing change.
Home lists only active projects and counts them; Find a project keeps typing and Esc working while ↑↓ choose.
Sheets, feedback, and project moving have a cleaner, easier-to-read look that matches the December design.
Finding a project now highlights the letters you typed and lets you step through the matches with the arrow keys. Project answers cite their meetings with shorter times.
Choosing more files while an import is running no longer interrupts it, and moving to another meeting while a change to its earlier meetings saves now shows the new meeting correctly.
A meeting's duration in the sidebar no longer cuts off beside a long project name, and VoiceOver now names the sidebar Meetings.

At narrow window widths, a meeting's header keeps people's names in view: the date and length shorten first. The list of people also opens slightly lower, under its button, and lines up with the design.
If your microphone drops out just as you switch to another one, the recording now moves to the one you chose instead of saying it heard nothing.
The first-run setup page is clearer: each step now says what it does, shows its progress, and lines up the way the design draws it.

The Home screen's search icon, All Meetings menu, settings gears and Record button now match the design more closely, and in dark mode the Coming up and Recent cards are the same shade without an outline.
You can now tick off, reword or dismiss a meeting's action items, see who owns each one, and find them as you left them next time you open the app.
During a recording you can go back to Home and return to your meeting at any time. When the sidebar is hidden, a toolbar button brings it back.
The Projects find shows no outer focus ring, the project title's ••• is smaller, and the Ask bar's send arrow is thinner.
The About, update, and What's New windows have a cleaner, easier-to-read look that matches the rest of the app.
The recording widget has a clearer new look: a dark card, level bars, each speaker in their own colour, and older lines that fade.
A meeting summary held up by a new recording now finishes later instead of staying missing.
A meeting's Summary shows its thumbs at rest, and the speaker-naming card opens below the turn it names.
When you name a speaker in a meeting that came from a calendar invitation, the card now lists the people who were invited, so you can pick the right name.
If a meeting starts while the update window is open, the window now says the update will wait, then offers it again when you're done.
During a recording, the Full widget now shows two rows for each speaker, so you can read the words just said.
An archived project keeps its last summary, so you can still read where things stood when you archived it.
Pressing Quit twice when your notes can't be saved now keeps the recording going, instead of ending it and leaving Auldera open.
View > Back and ⌘[ from a project's Ask tab now return to the project instead of Home.
When you stop a recording, the meeting no longer briefly says it was interrupted while its summary is being written.

Project pages and the Projects page have a "more" menu at the top right, next to Record. On a project it holds Rename, Color, Rewrite Summary, Archive and Delete; on the Projects page it holds New Project and the sort order.
The sidebar now keeps your upcoming meetings in view while you browse all projects.
Back from a project's Ask tab now returns to the project instead of Home.
When resetting sign-in cannot start because you are signing out, Auldera Enhanced and Sync keep working, and your Enhanced choice stays on.
The Projects section in Settings is now titled Projects, or the word you chose for projects, instead of Projects and Tags.
A meeting you stop just before starting another, or whose wrap-up card can't load, now still finishes its notes.
After stopping a recording on a wide window, the meeting page now switches to a single reading column with Notes, Brief, and Transcript tabs.
After you stop recording, the moments you pinned are listed above your notes. Remove any you don't need, or keep them all, in one step.
An archived project now opens like any other. Press it on Home, in the find, or on the Projects page to read its meetings and ask about them. Its page says Archived and offers Unarchive.
While you record in a wide window, your meeting brief and the live transcript now share the space equally, with a Transcript heading over the transcript.
Edit > Undo and Redo now work in meeting notes and in a meeting's preparation.
A finished meeting's page now reads like the design: notes first, the summary with its action items, the transcript beside them, and a simpler way to name a speaker.
Pin the last 30 seconds of a recording to your notes from the new Pin button, the recording widget, or ⌘M. It adds a line with the time and what was just said.

Home now opens on your projects. You see your latest meetings at a glance, then your most recently active projects with a find box, sorting, and Show All. Tomorrow's meetings fold into one line, and the reminder offer can be dismissed.
VoiceOver now announces a checklist in your notes as a list, with its number of items.
A recording that wasn't on your calendar now says so on its Brief tab, instead of showing a blank page.
After you stop a recording, the live summary stays on screen while the full summary is written, and the full one replaces it in place.

Projects in the sidebar now opens a page of all your projects. Each shows what's happening, when you last met, and what's next. You can find, sort and switch to archived projects, and review meetings that aren't in a project yet.

The notes field now styles your Markdown as you type: bold, italic, bullets, numbered lists and checklists draw in place, and a Format bar and keyboard shortcuts apply them. Your notes are still stored as plain text.

During a meeting, the Brief tab now shows what happened last time (the summary's opening and its next steps) and the meetings before that with one line each, and Show All lists every earlier meeting by month.
During a recording, the live summary is calmer and easier to scan: a small "Summary · Updating live" label sits over the points so far.
Back and Forward arrows at the top left of the window take you to where you came from and back again, also with ⌘[ and ⌘].
When you open a saved meeting, the line under its title now shows the same date and time it showed when the recording stopped.
A project's Ask answer now names the date of each meeting it quotes, beside the meeting name and the time in the recording.
After you stop a recording, the line under its title shows when it began and how long it ran. An upcoming meeting's project button shows just the project's name.
A meeting now has Notes, Brief and Transcript views under its title. Your preparation and what earlier meetings left are on Brief; your notes come first.
A project's page now lists its meetings, each with a one-line summary, beside where things stand, and the sidebar keeps every meeting in view.
The recording widget has a Minimal and a Full size in Settings. Full, the default, shows the last three lines of the transcript under the timer.
Every meeting page now starts the same way: the title, then the project (click it to change it), the date, time and length, and who was there, on one line.
The sidebar now has Home and Projects rows, shows each meeting's project as a link you can open, and keeps Send Feedback and Settings at the bottom.

A project's Ask tab is easier to read: the answer appears as one paragraph, with each quote it rests on listed underneath with the meeting, the time and a play button. Suggested questions and the question box now sit at the bottom of the page.
A meeting's header names up to three people and puts the rest behind an "and N others" button that lists everyone.
On a project's Overview, type a question in the "Ask about" bar and press Return to get the answer on the Ask tab. ⌘K now puts the cursor in that bar.
Home's Coming up is easier to scan: it shows up to five meetings today and three tomorrow, with a quiet Show More for the rest of each day.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2765)
release_notes: No customer-facing change. Routine CI defers unrelated broad suites to full-main validation and records positive non-native functional failures for cadence repair.
Searching your meetings now also finds the project a meeting belongs to. Search keeps working when your projects can't be read, and a search with no results says what you searched for and where.
Meetings in other languages show live text as you record, and a more accurate transcript replaces it soon after you stop.
Updating models leaves a working speech model in place, so the next time you open Auldera you can record without a long wait.
Stopping a recording in a large library finishes sooner when a search is open.
The recording indicator disappears after you stop, so it no longer suggests that recording continues while notes save.
Stopping a recording no longer waits for background speaker processing of older meetings.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2743)
release_notes: Recording starts sooner and keeps your opening words.
Summaries can update while you record on supported Macs, then refresh when you stop.
Summaries download in the background during setup, so you can start recording sooner and check or cancel the download from Home.
You can skip the Audio test to record your microphone, then set up call recording later.
Starting a recording begins right away instead of waiting for the on-device summary model to finish loading in the background.

Meeting pages are cleaner: a finished or live meeting shows its Summary, your notes, the transcript and Ask, without topic lists, thread links, commitment cards or the topic-model download. The meeting list on the left has a little more room.

On a Zoom call with one other person, speech that Auldera could not match to a name while recording now shows that person's name after you stop, shown dimmed until you confirm it, instead of a separate numbered speaker.
Suggested questions in Ask now appear as soon as a meeting's Summary is ready, without closing and reopening the meeting.
If you record a meeting before your Mac has a summary model, its summary now writes itself as soon as the model finishes downloading. Until then the meeting page says it is getting summaries ready.
Summaries of long Zoom meetings now start about a minute sooner after you stop recording.
A meeting summary that briefly can't reach the Enhanced service now keeps retrying instead of silently giving up.
You can now play the exact moment a quote in an Ask answer comes from. Press Play under the quote, and Stop to end it. When the audio for a quote is no longer on your Mac, Ask says so.

Remember this voice now appears for a speaker Zoom has named, even when their first line was named by Zoom directly. Confirming a name Zoom suggested now keeps all of that speaker's lines together when you rename them later.
First setup now offers an optional way to import transcripts from Zoom, Otter, Granola, or Markdown files, so your earlier meetings are in Auldera before your first recording.
After you allow calendar access the first time you open Auldera, your calendars now appear right away. You no longer have to quit and reopen the app.
Choose a Project when importing transcripts. The open Project is selected for you, or you can choose No project.
Ask now shows the exact words each answer comes from, with who said them and when, right under the answer. You no longer hover to see them. When part of an answer had no source, Ask says so.
Stopped Enhanced Project Summaries from repeatedly retrying in the background when an account is signed out, out of usage allowance, or missing access.

On a smaller Mac that runs low on memory during a meeting, Auldera now frees its on-device model within seconds, even when another summary is using it, and still names your topics when you stop recording.

You can now import a whole folder of Granola, Otter, Zoom or Markdown transcripts at once. Auldera picks the format and reads each meeting’s title and date from the file, then tells you how many meetings it imported, how many it already had, and which files it couldn’t read.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2690)
release_notes: Asking a question about a long meeting on your Mac now waits for the on-device model to finish reading the meeting instead of giving up after 29 seconds, and the wait says Reading the meeting… while it works.
Starting a recording no longer competes with a Project Summary refresh for memory, so recording stays smooth on Macs with less memory. The summary catches up after you stop.

The meeting page's sidebar now looks like Home: Coming up is grouped by day, and each meeting has one button to record, plus a gear for the rest. A new Home button beside the sidebar button takes you back to Home, and Command-[ steps back to your list.
The app icon and the install window now share Auldera's warm brown look.
A meeting's summary no longer waits indefinitely for speaker labels. After a minute it finishes with the labels it has, and recording a new meeting is never held up.

When you record a Zoom meeting, Auldera can now post a short notice in the meeting chat so others know the call is being recorded. You can skip it each time, copy it to paste yourself, or turn it off in Settings.
No user-facing change; this adds test coverage only.
Your meetings stay on your Mac: Auldera no longer uploads recordings or transcripts after a meeting. Settings now lists what still leaves your Mac.
None. No change to the app; this only changes which release-lane commit the nightly runs.
Recordings can free memory under severe memory pressure and still finish their summaries after Stop. Hosted recordings release unused local model memory.
After you name a speaker, a meeting's summary and copied summary use the new name right away, without asking you to rewrite it.
After you update models in Settings, Auldera is ready to record as soon as the download finishes. Record and automatic meeting start work again without restarting the app.
If you already have meetings and still need to finish setting up recording, All Meetings now shows the setup steps, including the audio test, so you can finish and start recording.
Opening a meeting from Home and coming back is quick again, even with a thousand meetings.
During a recording, the transcript now sits beside your notes as a second page on a wide window, and a Notes and Transcript switch under the title swaps between them on a narrower one.
Opening a meeting is quicker, especially in a large library, because the meeting now draws once instead of several times.
Dogfood builds: Home paints a large library as fast with UI replay on as with it off.
Coming up is simpler: each meeting has one button to record (Join and Record when there's a call link), and a gear that's always there for the rest, including joining without recording.
None. Dogfood diagnostics record each hosted model request in full.
On the dogfood Mac, signing in now syncs your meetings and your title, notes and speaker edits with your account, and signing out stops all syncing.
The setup checklist lines up in one column at every window width, and a finished step shows a single check mark.
When the window is wide, a meeting's transcript now sits beside your notes as a second page instead of a side panel, and transcript options sit next to the Notes and Transcript switch.
Auldera has a warmer look: clay-toned backgrounds and a rich brown accent replace the green, and alerts now stand out in amber.
Auldera can remember a speaker's voice and suggest their name in later meetings. Manage remembered voices in Settings, Recording.
First-time setup, the empty home page and home's problem notices have a calmer, more consistent look. Setup's buttons now match the rest of home, and both kinds of problem notice look the same.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2655)
release_notes: Pointing at a summary topic or suggestion no longer makes the page jump. The thumbs appear beside it, and the reasons open once you pick one.
Download the new on-device speaker model from Settings. Speaker labels keep working if the download fails.
Not filed: the review note on the production archive's write atomicity (no defect named).

None for people using the app. Dogfood builds upload each meeting's bundle under its settlement, keyed by the bundle's inventory. A library migrated to the new schema keeps a copy of the previous one beside it.
Live suggestions and meeting topics now read as a clean list instead of stacked grey boxes, with less empty space between them.
Live meetings and preparation pages have clearer titles and headings, with simpler meeting actions.

The home page's upcoming meetings now read like a calendar, with each day's date beside its meetings and tomorrow's set quieter, and past meetings show a letter tile and their time at the end of the row.
Meeting pages have a calmer, book-like look with a Notes and Transcript switch under the title, Record sits at the top of the sidebar, and Send Feedback is back at its foot.
Home now shows your next working day's meetings under today's, so you can see what's coming once today is done. Each meeting row also has a … button that opens its actions without right-clicking.

When a long meeting runs low on memory on a smaller Mac, live topic naming now gives up within seconds instead of stalling for minutes, frees its memory, and your topics are still named when you stop recording.
Send Feedback's meeting option now says it includes the meeting's summary and Ask history.
Topics in a meeting you just stopped now finish getting their titles, even when your Mac is low on memory.
Long meetings are more responsive when windows redraw or resize.
Speaker labels cover more of a meeting's speech when short pauses leave gaps in voice detection.
In saved meetings, Change speaker and Listen no longer cover the speaker's name or the transcript text, including with long names and larger text sizes.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2615)
release_notes: Transcript turns are easier to follow: each speaker's name has its own colour with a matching rule beside their words, and live transcripts no longer show gaps between words.
What's New no longer shows empty filler lines, so every entry you see is a real change.

Search meetings by person, date, or tag from a single search bar in the sidebar, view upcoming calls and past meetings in a cleaner timeline layout, and drag to resize the sidebar and live transcript feed.
Transcripts read more cleanly: the flag button appears only on the sentence you point at, and sentences no longer have gaps between them.

The upcoming meeting page is calmer. Your prep and open items read as a simple list, you can add a question with one click, the header shows when the meeting starts, and less-used actions moved to the … menu.
If a Mac was removed from your account, signing in again on it now works, without first resetting sign-in.
Speaker detection is less likely to combine different voices into one speaker.

entries.title: Auldera 0.1.0 (2606)
release_notes: You can rename a speaker named from Zoom in the transcript, or clear the name to use their Zoom name again.
The meeting-bundle note in private-beta Settings now matches the updated Privacy Policy.
Dogfood builds can now turn on nightly builds in Settings > Updates to get the latest changes every night.
Dogfood builds now install nightly updates only after opting in to nightly updates; certified builds stay on the beta channel.
If you quit Auldera before a meeting's summary could be written, the summary is now written the next time you open the app.
An open meeting page showing Previous context no longer keeps re-reading your library every few seconds, so Auldera uses much less CPU while idle.
While a meeting is recording, your notes, running summary, and a two-line live transcript feed appear together on one page, with the recording timer and Stop button in the top bar.
Prepare for your next meeting with a clearer page and a prominent Join and record button.

When Zoom speaker evidence identifies who spoke in a diarized cluster, the transcript now shows that participant's name in a dimmed style while keeping Speaker N in plain-text copies and exports until you confirm a name.
Sign in to Auldera in your browser using Apple or email, then return to the Mac app.

Each finished meeting now opens as one continuous page with your summary, decisions, next steps, open questions, notes, and inline Ask answers in a single column, plus a top-bar button to show or hide the transcript.
The meeting list now stays beside your notes down to compact window sizes and switches cleanly between the list and your meeting in narrow windows, with a simpler toolbar at the top of each meeting.
Speaker detection resumes after a new recording or an abandoned start, with its progress shown in the transcript.
When your Mac runs low on memory during a meeting, live topics no longer wait minutes for their titles. They get their names when the meeting ends instead.
Diagnostics from a long meeting now upload in the same day instead of waiting until the next, and a signed-in Mac keeps uploading even when the signed-out allowance is used up.
Windows and menus have a warmer, easier-to-read look.

The private beta's Zoom names step and detailed-logging note now say that your meeting bundle, including detailed logs and Zoom names, uploads automatically after each meeting once you are signed in. Detailed logging stays on or off exactly as you left it, and nothing asks you again.
When you start a new recording while the last meeting's summary is still being written, or right after you stop, that summary now finishes afterward instead of being lost.
If Auldera can't renew your sign-in, Settings now tells you and offers a one-click way back. Sync keeps working through a brief sign-in hiccup.

The private beta now tells you, when you sign in and in Settings, that it will upload each meeting you record, with its audio, after the meeting finishes. It lists what is included, says other people in your meeting are part of it, and explains how long it is kept and how deleting a meeting removes it.
